title: Finite-dimensional commutative Hopf algebras are self-injective
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A commutative Hopf $k$-algebra here means a unital commutative $k$-algebra $A$ with $k$-algebra maps $\Delta_A:A\to A\otimes_k A$, $\epsilon_A:A\to k$, $S_A:A\to A$ such that $(\Delta_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\Delta_A)\Delta_A$, $(\epsilon_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\epsilon_A)\Delta_A=1_A$, and $\mu_A(S_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=\mu_A(1\otimes S_A)\Delta_A=\eta_A\epsilon_A$, under the usual tensor unit and associativity identifications; $\mu_A$ and $\eta_A$ are multiplication and unit. Tensor products are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Let $H$ be such a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra admitting a finite $k$-vector-space basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For arbitrary $H$-modules $U,V$, every injective $H$-linear map $j:U\to V$ and every $H$-linear map $f:U\to H$ admit an $H$-linear map $g:V\to H$ with $g\circ j=f$. No finite-generation hypothesis is imposed on $U$ or $V$.

source.place: Bichon, arXiv:2301.05480v2, section 3, first paragraph: finite-dimensional Hopf algebras are self-injective. Read online at https://arxiv.org/html/2301.05480v2; local document WANTED in report.md. This is the injective-module extension formulation of that assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-hopf-frobenius-form] to $H$, with its given finite basis and Hopf structure. Choose $\lambda:H\to k$ such that $\Phi:H\to\operatorname{Hom}_k(H,k)$, $\Phi(a)(h)=\lambda(ha)$, is bijective. It is $k$-linear because multiplication and $\lambda$ are $k$-linear in each relevant variable. In particular an element of $H$ is uniquely determined by all the numbers $\lambda(ha)$, $h\in H$.

source.place: Section 3, first paragraph, self-injectivity assertion; agent proof by a Frobenius functional and extension of a field-linear functional. Local document WANTED.

proof.text: Regard $U,V$ as $k$-vector spaces by restriction of scalars. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector] with the empty independent set choose a basis $B$ of $U$. The set $j(B)$ is independent: applying injectivity of $j$ to a finite relation gives the corresponding relation in $B$. Use the same node to extend $j(B)$ to a basis $C$ of $V$. Assign the value $\lambda(f(b))$ to $j(b)$ and zero to every basis vector in $C\setminus j(B)$. Unique finite basis expansions define a $k$-linear map $t:V\to k$, and expansion in $B$ gives $t(j(u))=\lambda(f(u))$ for all $u\in U$.

source.place: Section 3, first paragraph, self-injectivity assertion; agent proof by a Frobenius functional and extension of a field-linear functional. Local document WANTED.

proof.text: For $v\in V$ the formula $h\mapsto t(hv)$ is $k$-linear, so bijectivity of $\Phi$ defines a unique element $g(v)\in H$ by $\lambda(hg(v))=t(hv)$ for every $h\in H$. For $v,w\in V$ and $a\in H$, evaluate at any $h\in H$: $\lambda(hg(v+w))=t(hv)+t(hw)=\lambda(h(g(v)+g(w)))$, and $\lambda(hg(av))=t((ha)v)=\lambda((ha)g(v))=\lambda(h(ag(v)))$. Injectivity of $\Phi$ gives $g(v+w)=g(v)+g(w)$ and $g(av)=ag(v)$. Thus $g$ is $H$-linear.

source.place: Section 3, first paragraph, self-injectivity assertion; agent proof by a Frobenius functional and extension of a field-linear functional. Local document WANTED.

proof.text: For $u\in U$ and $h\in H$, $H$-linearity of $j,f$ and the identity for $t$ give $\lambda(hg(j(u)))=t(hj(u))=t(j(hu))=\lambda(f(hu))=\lambda(hf(u))$. Injectivity of $\Phi$ gives $g(j(u))=f(u)$. This proves the extension condition. The bases in step 2 may be infinite; all expansions used there are finite sums, so no finite-generation hypothesis on $U$ or $V$ was used.
